node-1.label: Tender, enlarging scalp lesion present for 6 months

node-2.label: Patient is a 74-year-old man with a history of multiple squamous cell carcinomas treated with Mohs micrographic surgery

node-3.label: Physical examination revealed a 5-mm bright pink, dome-shaped papule with overlying vessels at the crown of the scalp, with no purulent discharge or overlying skin changes

why.why: The pathologist's analysis reinforces that the biopsy histology and immunohistochemistry establish a malignant neoplasm. Negative STAT6 additionally excludes solitary fibrous tumor, and the negative epithelial, melanocytic, and vascular markers exclude carcinoma, melanoma, and angiosarcoma. This further strengthens the malignant skin tumor hypothesis, raising confidence from 0.97 to 0.98.

The biopsy histology explicitly demonstrates a malignant neoplasm with hyperchromatic nuclei, mitoses, and necrosis, which effectively excludes a benign skin lesion/tumor. The prior possibility based on a dome-shaped papule is no longer tenable, so confidence is reduced from 0.18 to 0.01.

Biopsy reveals a dermal-based neoplasm with malignant features and no evidence of an inflammatory or infectious process; combined with the absence of purulent discharge, this refutes the inflammatory/infectious lesion hypothesis. Confidence is reduced from 0.10 to 0.01.

node-7.label: Biopsy shows dermal-based neoplasm with perivascular proliferation, hyperchromatic nuclei, mitoses, and necrosis

node-8.label: Immunohistochemistry shows diffuse SMA positivity and negative epithelial, melanocytic, and vascular markers

node-9.label: Smooth muscle-derived malignant neoplasm (smooth muscle sarcoma)

why.why: The pathologist's analysis confirms a smooth-muscle malignancy: diffuse SMA positivity with negative epithelial, melanocytic, vascular, and STAT6 markers excludes carcinoma, melanoma, angiosarcoma, and solitary fibrous tumor. Histology and immunohistochemistry together establish the smooth muscle sarcoma hypothesis, increasing confidence from 0.85 to 0.93.

The pathologist's analysis notes that loss of desmin, h-caldesmon, calponin, and smooth muscle myosin supports atypical leiomyosarcoma as a variant of smooth muscle sarcoma. This specific immunophenotypic finding directly supports the atypical diagnosis, increasing confidence from 0.55 to 0.75.
